title: Blue Apron Loses Money Every Year and Soon You Can Own Stock In It
summary: Blue Apron, the meal kit delivery service, has filed for its initial public offering (IPO) aiming to raise $100 million despite consistently incurring net losses, including $52 million in the first quarter of 2017. While the company has seen revenues grow significantly, these losses are attributed to increased expenditures, particularly a large marketing budget, as it seeks to finally turn a profit in a competitive market.

title: Oklahoma City's Paycom makes Forbes' Fast Tech 25 list
summary: Paycom Software Inc., an Oklahoma City-based company, has been ranked fourth on Forbes' 2017 Fast Tech 25 list, recognizing America's fastest-growing publicly traded technology companies. This marks Paycom's first appearance on the list, placing it ahead of major tech players like Amazon, PayPal, and Alphabet Inc. The company achieved this recognition due to its human capital management technology and strong sales growth, with 2016 revenue of $329.1 million.

title: Lululemon CEO: The Future of Retail Is Bright
summary: Lululemon CEO Laurent Potdevin expresses an optimistic view on the future of retail, despite industry challenges posed by e-commerce. He acknowledges the need for evolution in the sector and highlights Lululemon's strategy of expanding both its physical store footprint and its e-commerce business, alongside international growth and catering to the men's market. Potdevin's perspective contrasts with other retail executives who are more pessimistic about the current landscape.

title: Blackstone sells Logicor to China Investment Corporation for 12.25 billion euro
summary: Private equity group Blackstone has agreed to sell European warehouse firm Logicor to China Investment Corporation (CIC) for 12.25 billion euros, marking the biggest private equity real estate deal in Europe on record. This sale solidifies China's role in European private equity exits and scuppered plans for Logicor's London IPO. Logicor, founded by Blackstone in 2012, is the largest owner of European logistics and distribution properties, benefiting from the e-commerce boom.

title: Vimeo, Amazon Among Companies Joining Upcoming Protest To Defend Net Neutrality
summary: Vimeo, Amazon, Reddit, and Kickstarter are among dozens of major tech companies participating in a "Battle For The Net" protest on July 12 to defend net neutrality. This large-scale effort, led by activist group Fight For The Future, aims to oppose the FCC's proposal to strip away legal protections for net neutrality. The protest draws parallels to the 2012 internet blackout against SOPA, with companies like Vimeo emphasizing the importance of an open internet for creators.

title: Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE), an eight step quick history
summary: This article provides an eight-step history of Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) since its split in November 2015, detailing its strategic divestitures and acquisitions. It highlights how HPE refocused on core corporate and enterprise clientele, strengthening its server, storage, and networking offerings through key moves in high-performance computing, cloud analytics, security, hyper-converged infrastructure, and flash storage. The strategic changes aimed to make HPE a more "laser focused" organization to meet enterprise IT demands.

title: Lithonia Lighting Recalls to Repair Ceiling Light Fixtures Due to Impact Hazard
summary: Lithonia Lighting is recalling approximately 5,600 LBL4W model ceiling light fixtures manufactured between February 2016 and March 2017. The plastic diffuser lens on these fixtures can detach and fall, posing an impact hazard, though no injuries have been reported. Consumers should remove the existing lens and contact Lithonia Lighting for a free replacement lens to repair the unit.

title: Amazon Has Another Perk for Its Prime Members
summary: Amazon has introduced a new rewards program called Amazon Prime Reload, offering Prime members 2 percent back on Amazon purchases when they add funds to an online gift card. This initiative aims to encourage more purchases through its e-commerce site and attract new Prime subscribers. The program builds on Amazon's success with Prime, which sees members spend significantly more than non-members annually, and supports its strategic goal to grow its market share.

title: Amazon teams with Outfront Media and Rapport for largest Times Square advertising installment ever
summary: Amazon, in partnership with Outfront Media and Rapport, unveiled the largest advertising installment ever in Times Square, a 79-foot-tall Amazon Echo replica. This installation is part of Amazon Music’s "Music Unites" campaign, inspired by John Lennon and Yoko Ono's billboard campaign, featuring iconic lyrics in 15 cities globally. The giant Amazon Echo will be on display through June 25th, leveraging Times Square's high visibility for an impactful advertising presence.

title: Walmart maintains top Fortune 500 spot for 5th straight year
summary: Walmart topped Fortune's annual list of the top 500 U.S. companies by revenue for the fifth straight year. The article highlights Amazon's ascent, other major retailers' rankings, and how companies like Walmart and CVS are adapting to the evolving retail landscape driven by e-commerce and shifting consumer preferences. It also notes the aggregate economic impact of Fortune 500 companies.

title: Jessica Alba’s Honest Co. To Sell Goods on Amazon.com
summary: Jessica Alba's Honest Co. will begin selling its products on Amazon.com this month as part of a broader omnichannel strategy to expand its brand presence. The move aims to make the brand more relevant online, where consumer spending is increasingly gravitating, and complements its existing brick-and-mortar distribution in stores like CVS Health and Target. Honest Co. CEO Nick Vlahos sees Amazon as a key growth opportunity, especially given the ease of shipping its shelf-stable products.

title: Newegg makes big global push
summary: Newegg announced plans to expand its online electronics retail operations to dozens of new countries across Asia Pacific, Europe, Latin America, and the Middle East, aiming to reach customers in 50 countries. This global push, operating in beta, includes country-specific storefronts, local sellers, and native-language customer support. The move comes as Newegg faces stiff competition, particularly from Amazon, and seeks growth opportunities abroad by offering services to international marketplace sellers.

title: PG&E’s Bolt of Energy
summary: This article profiles Geisha Williams, the first Latina CEO of a Fortune 500 company, PG&E Corp. It details her journey from Cuba as a child to leading California's largest utility, focusing on her efforts to embrace renewable energy, modernize the grid, and navigate the complex challenges facing the power industry. The piece highlights her role in transforming PG&E into a leader in clean energy and her strategic vision for its future as a grid administrator.

title: 3 Cheap Fidelity Sector ETFs That Are Soaring – FDIS, FHLC, FSTA
summary: This article highlights three Fidelity sector ETFs (FDIS, FHLC, FSTA) that offer low fees and strong performance. It explains that Fidelity's 11 sector ETFs are the cheapest in the market, even compared to Vanguard, charging 0.084% annually. The article details each ETF's holdings, performance, and investment appeal, noting their suitability for cost-conscious investors seeking exposure to specific market segments like consumer discretionary, healthcare, and consumer staples.

title: How to Short Technology Stocks with ETFs
summary: The technology sector has shown signs of losing steam due to overvaluation concerns and profit-taking, leading investors to consider short positions. This article explores several ETFs that offer inverse exposure to the tech sector for investors looking to capitalize on a bearish outlook. It highlights ETFs with varying inverse exposures, including those focusing on the broader tech sector and the semiconductor industry, noting their suitability for short-term traders.

title: How Amazon could change your Whole Foods
summary: Following Amazon's $13.7 billion acquisition of Whole Foods Market, this article explores various ways Amazon could transform the grocery chain. Potential changes range from enhanced online ordering and delivery options to incorporating technology like touchscreen displays and cashier-free shopping, aiming to broaden customer appeal, lower prices, and improve efficiency. The article also discusses how Amazon's buying power and tech expertise could address Whole Foods' "Whole Paycheck" reputation and offer a better selection and customer service.

title: Amazon shakes up the grocery business with its $13.7-billion deal to buy Whole Foods
summary: Amazon announced its acquisition of Whole Foods Market for $13.7 billion, a move expected to significantly disrupt the U.S. grocery industry. This major purchase is anticipated to lead to lower prices and increased technological integration, benefiting consumers and pressuring rival supermarket chains. The deal sent grocery stock prices tumbling while Whole Foods and Amazon shares rose.

title: Amazon buying Whole Foods for $13.7 billion
summary: Amazon announced its acquisition of Whole Foods for $13.7 billion, valuing the grocer at $42 a share, a move that would make the combined company the seventh-largest food retailer in the U.S. The deal, which raised Amazon's stock by 3 percent, is expected to face regulatory scrutiny and has sparked discussions about potential impacts on competitors, shoppers, and workers. Despite concerns, an Amazon spokesperson indicated no layoffs are planned as a result of the merger.

title: Grocery stocks tank as ‘Amazon effect’ strikes fear in investors
summary: Shares of various grocery retailers experienced significant declines on Friday after Amazon.com Inc. announced its acquisition of Whole Foods Market Inc. for $13.7 billion. This "Amazon effect" caused investors to fear increased competition in the grocery sector. Major companies like Kroger, Costco, Target, and Wal-Mart saw their stock prices fall as a result of Amazon's move into the industry.

title: Grocery stocks tank as ‘Amazon effect’ strikes fear in investors
summary: Grocery store stocks experienced a significant decline after Amazon.com Inc. announced its acquisition of Whole Foods Market Inc. for $13.7 billion. This "Amazon effect" caused shares of major grocery retailers like Kroger, Costco, Target, and Wal-Mart to drop sharply, reflecting investor fear about increased competition in the sector.

title: Amazon to buy Whole Foods for $13.7 billion, wielding online might in brick-and-mortar world
summary: Amazon.com Inc announced its acquisition of Whole Foods Market Inc for $13.7 billion, a move that signals a significant shift for the e-commerce giant into brick-and-mortar retail and could profoundly impact the struggling U.S. retail industry. The deal, priced at $42 per share, sent ripples through financial markets, causing a collective loss of $35 billion in market value for supermarket chains, food producers, payment processors, and shopping malls. Whole Foods' CEO John Mackey will remain in his role, and the company will continue to operate under its brand.

title: |How Insurance Giant Allstate Is Using Cloud Tech to Build New Businesses
summary: |Allstate, an 86-year-old insurance giant, is leveraging cloud technology to innovate and compete with startups. Through its CompoZed Labs unit, Allstate has dramatically sped up software development, allowing for quick testing and deployment of new services like an improved roadside assistance app. This strategic use of cloud-agnostic tools enables flexibility and fosters creativity within the company.

title: Behind the charts: Amazon’s incredible impact on the consumer discretionary sector
summary: Amazon, often considered a tech stock, is actually the largest component of the consumer discretionary sector, making up about 15 percent of the sector and 1.8 percent of the S&P 500. Its 32 percent share price rise this year has significantly driven the sector's performance, contributing about a quarter of its nearly 11 percent rise. However, Amazon's success has also negatively impacted traditional retailers within the same sector.

title: Wal-Mart to Vendors: Get Off Amazon’s Cloud
summary: Wal-Mart is reportedly demanding that some of its technology vendors discontinue using Amazon Web Services (AWS) for applications they build for the retailer. This move intensifies the rivalry between Wal-Mart and Amazon, especially following Wal-Mart's acquisition of Jet.com. The directive aims to reduce Wal-Mart's indirect reliance on its competitor's cloud infrastructure.

title: How Netflix Ticks: Five Key Insights From the Company’s New Corporate Culture Manifesto
summary: Netflix has updated its famous "freedom & responsibility" corporate culture document, offering new insights into the company's internal workings. The document emphasizes a "dream team" philosophy over perks, a strict "no brilliant jerks" policy, and a high-performance environment where only the best employees are retained. It also highlights Netflix's unusual approach to expenses, vacation time, and parental leave, stressing trust and responsibility over rigid rules.

title: Critics say Whole Foods deal would give Amazon an unfair advantage
summary: Critics argue that Amazon.com Inc.'s acquisition of Whole Foods Market Inc. should be blocked, claiming it gives Amazon an unfair head start in online grocery delivery. While antitrust experts anticipate regulatory approval due to Amazon's small grocery sales and Whole Foods' market size, critics believe Amazon's strengths in logistics and scale could lead to market domination similar to its impact on bookselling. They also raise concerns about potential "buyer power" and the leveraging of dominance from one market to another.

title: Kroger Has Bigger Problems -- Amazon Is Buying Whole Foods
summary: Kroger faces increased challenges following Amazon's acquisition of Whole Foods, exacerbating existing competitive pressures from German grocers Aldi and Lidl and a decline in same-store sales. Despite having navigated similar competitive landscapes in the past, the entry of Amazon into the grocery market creates new uncertainties for Kroger's future. The company is responding by cutting prices, expanding online sales capabilities, and implementing share buybacks to benefit shareholders.

title: Is Amazon getting too big?
summary: This article discusses whether Amazon is becoming too large and dominant across various industries like groceries, streaming video, books, clothing, and cloud computing. While Amazon is not dominant in every area, its vast ecosystem, particularly through its Prime subscription, raises concerns among observers about stifling competition and impacting suppliers, despite benefiting consumers with low prices and convenience. Critics question the long-term economic implications of one company acting as a "gatekeeper" in e-commerce.

title: After Launching E-Commerce, LVMH Invests in Online Fraud Startup
summary: After launching an e-commerce website for its numerous fashion brands, French luxury goods conglomerate LVMH Moët Hennessy Louis Vuitton has invested in Riskified, an e-commerce fraud prevention startup. LVMH joins other investors, including Capital One Financial Corp, in a new funding round totaling $33 million, which Riskified will use for global expansion and sales acceleration. The investment highlights the growing market for online fraud prevention as more consumers shop online.

title: The 50 Smartest Companies in 2017, According to MIT Experts
summary: MIT Technology Review released its annual list of the world's 50 smartest companies for 2017, based on business savvy and creative use of emerging technology. Nvidia topped the list for its AI software and growing AI businesses, with a valuation of $90.9 billion. The list also includes major companies like Apple and Facebook, alongside newcomers such as Face++, Carbon, and Desktop Metal.

title: Blue Apron slashes its IPO range
summary: Blue Apron has slashed the expected price range for its initial public offering (IPO) from $15-$17 per share to $10-$11 per share. This adjustment lowers the company's estimated valuation from $3.2 billion to $2.08 billion, with the IPO expected to price Wednesday and stock debut on Thursday. The meal-kit delivery service aims to raise approximately $292.7 million for working capital and general corporate purposes, despite never having turned a profit and facing increased competition and high subscriber churn rates.

title: Fubo TV: All the details on this sports-heavy streaming bundle
summary: FuboTV, initially a soccer-focused streaming service, has expanded to offer a wider range of cable channels with a strong emphasis on sports, announcing new channels from CBS and Scripps Networks and closing a $55 million investment round. This article details its channel lineup, regional sports coverage, DVR functionality, on-demand options, device support, video quality, and simultaneous stream restrictions. While praised for its sports focus, the service's app functionality and DVR limitations are noted as areas needing improvement.

title: Blue Apron stock edges up from the IPO price that fell far short of expectations
summary: Blue Apron's stock edged up 3.5% after its IPO, closing at $10.35, despite the company slashing its initial offering price to $10 a share from an expected $15-$17. This lower valuation reflects investor concerns about heightened competition in the meal kit market and Blue Apron's profitability challenges, even with nearly $800 million in revenue last year. The company faces stiff competition and a high customer churn rate, with many millennials canceling subscriptions due to cooking time and relatively high prices.

title: Amazon ‘will be a top 5 grocer in the U.S.’ with Whole Foods acquisition
summary: Experts predict that Amazon will become a top five U.S. grocer within the next five years following its $13.7 billion acquisition of Whole Foods Market Inc. The acquisition is seen as a strategic move by Amazon to sustain its growth by entering the grocery market. While Amazon may not aim to be the largest grocer, its focus will be on becoming a leading player in key cities.
